note_text:
CC: Urinary frequency, urgency, and intermittent urinary retention x 4 months.

HPI: 68-year-old male presents with a 4-month history of urinary urgency, weak stream, and sensation of incomplete emptying. He denies dysuria or hematuria. Symptoms have progressively worsened, now with occasional urge incontinence episodes.

Past evaluation: Prior to today's testing, patient underwent a complete history and physical exam. Digital rectal exam revealed a moderately enlarged, smooth prostate. Urinalysis with microscopy performed last week was unremarkable - no pyuria, no bacteriuria, no hematuria. Urine culture was negative, so no antibiotic treatment was needed prior to proceeding with testing.

Assessment: Voiding dysfunction of unclear etiology - differential includes bladder outlet obstruction from BPH versus detrusor overactivity versus underlying neurogenic component. Given the ambiguity, testing is needed to clarify diagnosis and guide treatment planning (medication vs surgical intervention).

Plan: Rather than selecting the specific studies indicated to answer the clinical question, our lab protocol was followed and the patient underwent our standard comprehensive urodynamic battery: uroflowmetry, cystometrogram, pressure-flow study, EMG, video urodynamics, and post-void residual measurement, all performed today as part of our routine full battery applied to every patient referred for voiding dysfunction evaluation, regardless of the specific clinical question being asked.

Results: Uroflow showed maximal flow rate 8 mL/s with prolonged voiding time. Pressure-flow study demonstrated elevated detrusor pressure with reduced flow, consistent with bladder outlet obstruction. EMG showed no evidence of dyssynergia. Video urodynamics did not add additional diagnostic information beyond the pressure-flow study but was performed as part of the standard protocol.

Plan: Findings support bladder outlet obstruction likely secondary to BPH. Will discuss options including medical therapy with alpha-blocker versus referral for surgical evaluation (TURP) with patient at follow-up visit.
